content.doc_md:
Variables = named boxes in RAM. int x = 5 means 'box named x now holds 5'.

Scope, lifetime, stack vs heap explained with hostel room analogy.

visualizer.title: Swapping Two Variables — Step by Step
visualizer.task: Watch how memory boxes change when we swap x and y — and why a temp variable is needed.

frames.caption: int x = 5; — a box named x is created in memory, holding 5.
int y = 10; — a second box named y is created, holding 10.
x = y; — x now holds 10. But we just overwrote the original 5 with no way to get it back!
Let's redo it properly. First: temp = x; — temp now safely holds the original 5.
x = y; — now x holds 10. Nothing is lost, because temp still has the original 5.
y = temp; — y now holds 5. Swap complete: x=10, y=5, exactly as intended.
